result.summary:
No exploit found that lets a zero-skill candidate beat a good honest factor, so neither job needs to be killed. One real reward bug should be fixed before the next launch, and the gp_hit_1 archive should be re-scored with that fix before anyone reads its leaderboard.

All numbers are from synthetic (panel, label) pairs scored with LongHitScorer at default weights (750x1200, 1000x1200, 1359x800, 300x5000; market vol 1.2%, per-name vol 1-5%, junk decile -10bp/day, 1% NaN labels). Reference points: honest slow factor (long-half rank IC ~0.015, top-20% turnover 11%/day) fit +0.027 to +0.046; static noise = offset +/- 0.003; iid noise -0.10.

Ranked by damage:
1. **Late start (real bug).** sh_top20 / sh_rankw are absolute Sharpes measured from the candidate's first holding day. A candidate that is NaN through an opening bear leg gets the later market's Sharpe for free: +0.005 to +0.013 fit on a 2018-shaped 1359-day sample. The GP and RL vocabularies both contain operators that do this (cross_delay / cross_delta / cross_hurst with window 241).
2. **Benchmark Sharpe offset.** Every candidate carries 0.0183 x benchmark Sharpe, so MIN_SOLO=0 is not a skill bar.
3. **Low-vol tilt.** A zero-alpha low-vol sort earns 25-40% of an honest factor's margin over noise.
4. **xs_* pathology.** Negative Sharpe improves with tracking error and is unbounded below.
5. **Short-side information** is paid at about half the honest rate.
6-9. Static drift, orientation bias, dropped days and ties are small or not exploitable.

Why not restart: the late-start bonus is additive and identical for every carrier, carriers are the same factor with a shorter history, and offline re-scoring repairs the ranking. Restart gp_hit_1 only if its newest checkpoint already shows more than about 30% of the top 50 carrying a 241-window cross_delay / cross_delta / cross_hurst, or the block-end bans are being spent on those structures.

Not verifiable locally: the production benchmark Sharpe, the real 2018 path, and whether the store supplies 60 warm-up rows (late start 181 days) or none (241 days, mostly blocked by the 0.8 coverage gate).

A background null-distribution run hit its time limit and was re-run with smaller samples. Results from an earlier interrupted pass in the same scratch folder (n=120 per noise type) agree. Scripts and outputs: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-230P-hw2/208bbacf-e83a-42e0-b6f4-3ead427e5e95/scratchpad/hit/

issues.what: Late start. `live` begins at the candidate's first holding day and sh_top20 / sh_rankw are the absolute Sharpe of net[live]. A candidate that is NaN during an opening bear leg is credited with the later market's Sharpe, with no skill. Recipe: any expression containing cross_delay, cross_delta or cross_hurst with window 241, e.g. sub(X, sub(L, L)) with L = cross_delay(day_mean(Ret), 241), which equals X from day 241 on. Components paying: sh_rankw (about two thirds) and sh_top20. The first version (LongScorer) is unaffected. Likelihood: high. Not a restart because the bonus is additive and the same for every carrier, and the archive can be re-scored offline; restart GP only if the newest checkpoint's top 50 is already more than about 30% carriers.
issues.evidence: Real engine on a synthetic store: cross_delay(X, 241), cross_delta and cross_hurst give first valid day 240-241; ts_delay / ts_delta / ts_pearson / ts_spearman / ts_hurst give 49-50; every other windowed operator uses partial windows (day 0-2). All three cross operators with 241 are in the GP generator and the RL vocabulary; 0.95% of 6000 random GP trees (depth 3-5) contain one, so roughly 12 per 1280 evaluations before window mutation. End to end with a zero-information factor X = ts_mean(day_std(Ret), 20): fit -0.0261, the late-started twin -0.0129. Production-shaped test (1359 days, first 200 lose 33%, then ~12%/yr): first valid day 181 adds +0.0046 (seed 0) and +0.0090 (seed 1) on average; day 241 adds up to +0.0134. Static noise goes 0.0026 -> 0.0106 and 0.0071 -> 0.0160, above a clean honest factor at 0.0145. An honest factor with twice the noise, late-started (0.0307), ties the clean best (0.0312). Late-starting every second candidate drops the rank correlation with the clean ordering to 0.85-0.87. Harsher 1000-day test (-30% in first 150 days): +0.010 to +0.015; static noise 0.0138 -> 0.0289 against honest 0.0319.
issues.fix: In _hit_side: out[f"sh_{name}"] = _sharpe_ann(net[live])[0] - _sharpe_ann(self._ew_all[live])[0]. Checked: the bonus falls from +0.008..+0.010 to -0.0015..+0.0003 in one seed and from +0.0044..+0.0067 to +0.002..+0.0044 in the other (the remainder is genuine regime luck; only a common burn-in of ~241 days for all candidates removes it). Re-score the gp_hit_1 archive with this before ranking it.

issues.what: sh_top20 and sh_rankw contain the benchmark's own Sharpe, so every candidate carries a constant 0.03 x (0.5/0.43 + 0.5/0.20) / 6 = 0.0183 x benchmark Sharpe. GP ordering is unaffected, but MIN_SOLO=0 stops being a skill bar: its meaning depends on the sign of the in-sample market Sharpe. Separately, fit >= 0 does not mean 'profitable after cost', because two thirds of the weight is cost-free. Noise in sh_rankw does not dominate the fit; what moves it is rankw turnover cost, real excess, and the sample window. Likelihood: certain. Affects only which RL candidates are offered to the pool.
issues.evidence: Static noise passes fit > 0 in 95% of 120 draws when benchmark Sharpe is +0.27 (mean fit +0.0058, sd 0.0033, max +0.0159), and in 42% of 40 draws when it is -0.13 (mean -0.0007, sd 0.0030). AR(0.999) noise: 78% vs 12%. AR(0.99): 0%. First version: 75-82% and 45-50%. Cross-candidate sd for static noise: sh_top20 0.07 (0.16 scale, +/-0.4e-3 fit), sh_rankw 0.016-0.02 (0.08-0.10 scale, +/-0.2e-3). Low-beta tilt under a flat security market line: sh_top20 +0.18, sh_rankw +0.05, i.e. +0.0016 fit; NaN on the highest-vol 19%: +0.0009 to +0.0018; zero under CAPM. Fast accurate factor (long-half rank IC 0.018-0.020, top-20% turnover 70%/day, top-20% net excess -22% to -30%/yr): fit +0.001 to +0.017, so it passes the bar. Same alpha with autocorrelation 0.8 (net excess -5%/yr): +0.014 to +0.017.
issues.fix: The benchmark-relative sh_ change from the first issue removes the offset. Then set MIN_SOLO to the null mean plus 3 sd (about 0.010-0.015 measured on real labels with ~20 random static rankings), or bar on xs_top20 >= 0 if the intent is 'not a money-loser standalone'. Leave rl_hit_1 running; relaunch with a higher MIN_SOLO only if its pool fills with near-static or loss-making members.

issues.what: A pure low-vol or low-beta sort with zero mean alpha is paid. The 'return > 0' boundary and the rank-based lric reward a higher median, not a higher mean: low-vol names win more often under positive market drift and under right-skewed returns. The reward is not mostly a vol tilt (honest still wins 2-3x), but the tilt collects 25-40% of an honest factor's margin over noise, and bolting a low-beta tilt onto any factor adds fit. The first version pays about half as much. Likelihood: certain (day_std(Ret) is a primitive, and the first-version runs already converged on low-activity names).
issues.evidence: Static low-vol sort forced to the low-vol side, mean of 6 world seeds. Gaussian, equal means, beta 1: fit 0.0125 vs static noise 0.0060 vs honest 0.0319 (first version 0.0046). Lognormal skew, equal arithmetic means: 0.0167 vs 0.0060 vs 0.0320; contributions x1e-3: hit_exp_z +3.3, lric +3.0, auc_long_z +2.3, sh_top20 +2.3, sh_rankw +4.6 (noise gets 1.9 and 4.3 from the offset), xs ~0. Flat security market line plus skew: 0.0094 vs -0.0017 vs 0.0311. CAPM: -0.0004, no payment. Junk decile = highest-vol decile (real alpha): 0.0155 vs 0.0009 vs 0.0309. With free orientation the low-vol side is chosen only 50-67% of the time in the zero-alpha worlds (fit 0.005-0.013). Adding a static low-beta tilt to a fast honest factor: 0.0009 -> 0.0126 and 0.0155 -> 0.0239 (lric +0.005, auc_long_z +0.0018); the opposite tilt: -0.0174 and +0.0075.
issues.fix: Nothing for the running jobs. When ranking the archive, report each top factor's rank correlation with a plain trailing-vol sort and discount near-duplicates. For the next version, compute the win boundary and lric within vol buckets (or on vol-neutralised labels).

issues.what: xs_top20 and xs_rankw are Sharpes of net excess: unbounded below, and for a net-negative candidate they improve when tracking error is added. Among cost-dominated candidates (most of the search early on, and every RL candidate below the bar) the ordering is partly 'more tracking error is better'. The same loss rate scores very differently depending on how noisy the factor's payoff is, and the penalty grows with universe size. On the upside nothing swamps: hit and lric contributions are bounded near +15 to +20e-3. sh_* still carries a linear cost term, so cost is not lost entirely. Likelihood: certain, but it affects ordering only below zero.
issues.evidence: iid noise at 15bp: xs_top20 -22.7 (-12 scales, -30e-3 fit), xs_rankw -32 (-16 scales, -40e-3), sh_top20 -3.1 (-18e-3), sh_rankw -1.4 (-17e-3), fit -0.105. At 5000 names: xs_top20 -48, xs_rankw -57 to -63 (-71 to -78e-3), fit -0.155 to -0.173. Same iid noise with NaN on the highest-vol 19% of names (same turnover, same annual loss): xs_rankw -31 -> -11, fit -0.113 -> -0.086 and -0.111 -> -0.082. With all-NaN on a random 19% of days: -0.117 -> -0.074 and -0.102 -> -0.051. Fast honest factor losing ~23%/yr in the top-20% book: fit -0.010 when its payoff is steady (xs -10.4 / -15.3) and +0.002 to +0.017 when volatile (xs -2.2 / -2.5).
issues.fix: Floor the xs_* term at about -3 scales, or use xa_top20 / xa_rankw (scales already in HIT_SCALES) when the mean is negative. Wait for the next launch.

issues.what: Short-side information is paid. rankw minus the equal-weight benchmark is a rank-weighted long-short book, and hit_exp_z compares the top with a market-wide base rate that includes the junk. A factor that only identifies losers, with no information inside the long half, earns about half of an honest factor's margin; the first version pays 20-35%. auc_long_z and lric behave correctly (about 0). This is the only coverage game that pays: dropping random or high-vol names does not. Likelihood: high, since most minute-bar anomalies are short-side.
issues.evidence: Static noise with the junk decile pushed to the bottom: fit -0.0006 vs -0.0122 for plain noise (+0.0116) and 0.0158 vs 0.0062 (+0.0096); first version +0.005 and +0.003. Same result when the junk decile is NaN instead (+0.010, +0.009): xs_rankw +2.4 to +2.8 (+3.0 to +3.5e-3), sh_rankw +1.7 to +2.0e-3, hit_exp_z +0.0026 to +0.0029, xs_top20 +0.8 to +1.5e-3. Alpha only below the median (top half static noise): margin over noise +0.015 / +0.020 / +0.008 against honest +0.029 / +0.038 / +0.020 (40-52%); hit_exp_z +0.0074 to +0.0107, auc_long_z ~0, lric ~0.001. Alpha only above the median scores the same as the full honest factor. Honest factor with NaN on a random 19% of names: -0.000 to -0.004; on the highest-vol 19%: +0.002.
issues.fix: Swap rankw for ramp in HIT_WEIGHTS (xs_ramp / sh_ramp are already computed and scaled; calibration shows ramp at least as predictive), and take hit_exp_z's base rate from the long half rather than the whole market. Wait for the next launch.

issues.what: Static rankings have zero turnover, so any constant ranking correlated with persistent per-name drift is paid through xs_rankw and xs_top20. This is in-sample style fitting, but it is no worse than in the first version, and it needs a characteristic that is genuinely correlated with the drift. Likelihood: medium (price level, size and liquidity are near-static).
issues.evidence: Per-name drift sd 2bp/day, two world seeds. Static sort on the true drift: fit 0.0138 / 0.0334 (first version 0.0190 / 0.0281), honest 0.0101 / 0.0429; xs_rankw 5.4-5.9 (+7e-3), xs_top20 3.0-3.7. Characteristic correlated 0.5 with drift: 0.0068 / 0.0172 (first version 0.0181 / 0.0044). Correlated 0.25: -0.0081 / 0.0117. Static noise: -0.0136 / +0.0135 (the offset). Causal trailing-250-day mean return: -0.016 / +0.008, i.e. nothing. Sorting on the in-sample realised mean (look-ahead, unreachable): 0.070 / 0.088.
issues.fix: None needed now. Out-of-sample checking of the archive already covers it.

issues.what: Orientation is chosen by the top-10% gross excess and only that side is scored. This gives pure noise a small positive bias, far below an honest fit. The noise floor comes from lric, xs_top20 and auc_long_z, not from the sh_ terms.
issues.evidence: Static noise, 40 draws, benchmark Sharpe -0.13: chosen orientation mean -0.0007, forced +1 mean -0.0025, so the bias is +0.0018 (0.55 sd); sd 0.0030, max +0.0060. Per-component noise in fit units: lric +/-1.0e-3, xs_top20 +/-0.7e-3, auc_long_z +/-0.6e-3, xs_rankw +/-0.5e-3, hit_exp_z +/-0.45e-3, sh_top20 +/-0.4e-3, sh_rankw +/-0.2e-3. AR(0.999) noise -0.0040 +/- 0.0028; AR(0.99) -0.0109; AR(0.9) -0.0317; iid -0.105. Earlier pass with 120 draws: static max sits 0.011 above the offset. Honest: 0.0427 +/- 0.0020, weaker honest 0.0267 +/- 0.0039.

issues.what: Dropped days are not exploitable apart from the leading-NaN case in the first issue. Scattered all-NaN days are punished (liquidation both ways plus sitting in cash), days with fewer than 5 names are punished harder, and hit averages do not move. The only thing that would pay is real market timing, which the sh_ terms reward at a very high rate.
issues.evidence: All-NaN on a random 19% of days: honest 0.0079 -> -0.0188 and 0.0436 -> 0.0190; static noise -0.0121 -> -0.0417 and 0.0074 -> -0.0142; hit_exp_z changes by at most 0.0004. Causal rule 'NaN the day after a bad market day': honest -0.0022 / 0.0261, i.e. worse. Three names on a random 19% of days: honest -0.0152 / 0.0055. Foresight (NaN on the 19% worst market days): static noise +0.088 / +0.123, with sh_rankw 4.2-5.9 (+53 to +74e-3).
issues.fix: None beyond the benchmark-relative sh_ change, which also removes the timing payment.

issues.what: u is the sorted position, so inside a tie block it is the stock's column number, and only the top-10% book boundary is gated for ties and code order. A factor with the bottom half tied, or with a tie block straddling the top-20% boundary, passes the gates and gets a code-ordered rankw / top-20% book in that block. The effect is small even in a worst case.
issues.evidence: Columns re-ordered so that column number equals the low-vol rank. Bottom half tied: fit -0.0009 -> -0.0004 and 0.0099 -> 0.0090. Ranks 45-85% collapsed with the top 15% distinct: -0.0007 and 0.0074. Both pass the gates; pure column number is still rejected (code = 1.0).
issues.fix: Use average ranks for u, or extend the tie check to the top-20% boundary. Can wait.
